claims.text: The starting alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
HfZrTiTa0.53 exhibits poor uniform deformability and rapid failure during room-temperature adiabatic dynamic loading.
The proposed intervention is dynamic deformation at approximately 10^3 s^-1 and about 77 K.
Cryogenic high-strain-rate loading will activate deformation twinning in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Cryogenic deformation will increase deformation-twin density in HfZrTiTa0.53.
Deformation twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Cryogenic conditions suppress the detrimental effect of adiabatic heating on strain hardening.
Reduced thermal activation at cryogenic temperature promotes twin nucleation and stability.
The cryogenically generated twins will increase strain-hardening.
Twin-mediated strain hardening will delay strain localization and failure.
Cryogenic dynamic loading will raise the yield strength by more than 10% relative to the quasi-static baseline.
Cryogenic dynamic loading will raise the compressive strength by more than 10% relative to the quasi-static baseline.
Cryogenic dynamic loading will produce a fracture strain higher than 13.5%.
Cryogenic dynamic loading will improve resistance to strain localization.
Cryogenic dynamic loading will increase impact-induced energy absorption.
The predicted effect is restricted to adiabatic loading near 10^3 s^-1 at cryogenic temperature and may not occur at slower rates or other temperatures.

contradictions.description: The predicted strength and ductility changes are defined relative to a quasi-static room-temperature baseline, whereas the matched experiment and falsification rule compare cryogenic dynamic specimens against room-temperature dynamic specimens. These are different comparators, so the experiment does not directly test all stated baseline-relative predictions.

The outcome is framed as increased energy absorption, but the measurement is described as energy absorption measured through 'energy release.' Absorbed and released energy are not interchangeable without an explicit energy-balance definition.
